The indictment of neighbor against neighbor continues through the verse after it before the row closes unchanged on oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6, שִׁבְתְּךָ֖ בְּת֣וֹךְ מִרְמָ֑ה בְּמִרְמָ֛ה מֵאֲנ֥וּ (oshb:Jer.9.5, byte tier) -- 'shivtekha betokh mirmah,' 'your dwelling is in the midst of deceit' -- before the title-stack koh-amar onset that follows, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.9.6 = web:Jer.9.7, byte tier). The second-person material recurring in this closing verse, שִׁבְתְּךָ֖ ('your dwelling'), is a suffix only, with no vocative, no imperative, and no second-person verb, so it does not meet the discourse-frame onset class and the verse stays inside this row's own close.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6, where a second-person suffix appears, was considered; it is rejected because the suffix alone carries no vocative, imperative, or verb, so it does not meet the discourse-frame onset class and the verse is kept inside this row's own close.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on a rhetorical question rather than a formula, oshb:Jer.9.11 = web:Jer.9.12, מִֽי הָאִ֤ישׁ הֶֽחָכָם֙ וְיָבֵ֣ן אֶת זֹ֔את (oshb:Jer.9.11, byte tier) — ‘mi ha-ish he-chakham veyaven et zot,’ ‘who is wise enough to understand this? who is he to whom the mouth of Yahweh has spoken.’ The answer, oshb:Jer.9.12 = web:Jer.9.13, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה עַל עָזְבָם֙ אֶת תּ֣וֹרָתִ֔י (oshb:Jer.9.12, byte tier) — ‘vayomer YHWH, al ozvam et torati,’ ‘Yahweh says, because they have forsaken my law’ — diagnoses the ruin named in the question, and the therefore-clause, oshb:Jer.9.14 = web:Jer.9.15, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֧י מַאֲכִילָ֛ם (oshb:Jer.9.14, byte tier) — ‘lachen koh amar YHWH tsevaot Elohei Yisrael, hineni ma'akhilam,’ ‘therefore thus says Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, behold, I will feed them’ — carries the same answer to its verdict rather than opening a fresh address. The row closes at web:Jer.9.16 = oshb:Jer.9.15 because web:Jer.9.17 = oshb:Jer.9.16 opens on its own koh-amar-plus-imperative onset, כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ (oshb:Jer.9.16 = web:Jer.9.17, byte tier) -- 'koh amar YHWH tsevaot, hitbonenu,' 'thus says Yahweh of Armies, consider.'
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The verdict beginning at 9.15 could open its own row as a fresh koh-amar onset, but it is grammatically the therefore-clause of the answer that begins at 9.13 rather than a new question-and-answer exchange, so the whole reply is kept as one unit.

current_row.device_notes: The passage argues in a question-and-answer shape closer to a covenant lawsuit than a direct announcement; it is carried under the judgment-oracle heading because it ends in the same punishment verdict, scattering and the sword, as the oracles around it, not a formal accusation addressed to a defendant. WEB formats the whole span without poetry lines, unlike the material on either side of it, a translation-layout fact carrying no evidential weight in either direction. A setumah opens the row at oshb:Jer.9.10, immediately before it, another falls at oshb:Jer.9.11 and oshb:Jer.9.13, and a petuchah closes it at oshb:Jer.9.15 — single-witness, WLC.
